data.content_ref: inline:The target's own counterconditions flag the answer as wrong under the conventional interpretation, yet the mechanism commits to $909 by paying the base $18 rate for all 47 hours. This inflates overtime-hour pay to $27 ($18 base + $9 premium) instead of the $27 overtime rate being applied only to hours beyond 40; equivalently, it computes base pay as if all 47 hours were regular, adding a premium on top, rather than computing 40×$18 + 7×$27. The counterexample condition explicitly notes the standard method yields $855, so the target fails the problem's intended calculation.
